summary.en: The house of the judge Ibn Luqman in Mansoura, where King Louis IX of France was held prisoner in 1250, now the Mansoura National Museum.
summary.ar: بيت القاضي ابن لقمان بالمنصورة، الذي سُجن فيه ملك فرنسا لويس التاسع عام 1250، ويضم اليوم متحف المنصورة القومي.

description.en: Dar Ibn Luqman takes its name from Fakhr al-Din Ibrahim ibn Luqman, the city’s judge in the thirteenth century. Its fame comes from the Seventh Crusade: after the Crusader army was defeated near Mansoura and at Fariskur in 1250, King Louis IX of France was captured and held in this house until his ransom was arranged. The building keeps the plan of a traditional town house around a central court with a wooden staircase. The ground-floor rooms, rebuilt as a single hall, present the history of the Crusades and the battle of Mansoura with paintings and medieval weapons. Upstairs is the room where the king is said to have been confined, furnished with a wooden bench and a large chair and dramatised by a life-size figure of Louis in chains with his guard, the eunuch Subayh. Verses mocking the defeated king are inscribed above the door. The house opened as a museum in 1960 and reopened in 2015 after restoration.
description.ar: تحمل دار ابن لقمان اسم فخر الدين إبراهيم بن لقمان، قاضي المدينة في القرن الثالث عشر الميلادي. واكتسبت شهرتها من الحملة الصليبية السابعة، فبعد هزيمة جيش الصليبيين قرب المنصورة وفي فارسكور عام 1250 أُسر ملك فرنسا لويس التاسع، واحتُجز في هذه الدار حتى جرى الاتفاق على فديته. يحتفظ المبنى المتواضع بتخطيط البيت التقليدي حول صحن أوسط يصعد منه سلم خشبي إلى الدور الثاني. وقد أُعيد بناء حجرات الدور الأرضي على هيئة قاعة واحدة تعرض تاريخ الحروب الصليبية ومعركة المنصورة بلوحات وأسلحة من العصور الوسطى. وفي الدور العلوي الحجرة التي يُقال إن الملك حُبس فيها، وبها أريكة خشبية وكرسي ضخم، ويجسد المشهدَ تمثالٌ بالحجم الطبيعي للويس مكبلًا وخلفه حارسه الطواشي صبيح. وتعلو الباب أبيات شعرية تسخر من الملك المهزوم. افتُتحت الدار متحفًا عام 1960، وأُعيد افتتاحها عام 2015 بعد ترميمها.

desc.en: The upper room where the captive king was held, with a life-size tableau.

curationNote: Dar Ibn Luqman houses the 'Mansoura National Museum' of the Fine Arts Sector (fineart.gov.eg IDs=9). Ministry of Culture (Fine Arts Sector) museum, not SCA: the SCA Arab-tier rule does not apply. Prices 5 Egyptian / 3 Egyptian student / 10 foreign and free groups from the undated official fineart.gov.eg visitor page (live official page, D6); no 2025-2026 price decision found, and the page also shows outdated hours, so prices should be confirmed by phone. No foreign-student price published. Ramadan: sector-wide 10:00-14:00 (Ramadan 2026 statement), Mon/Fri closed as in the normal week. No last entry published. Hours conflict: the fineart.gov.eg visitor page says 10:00-16:00 except Monday and Friday; the Fine Arts Sector's summer-2026 statement (youm7, 4 Jun 2026) gives 09:00-16:00, closed Friday and Monday, for 'the other specialised museums such as' Rateb Seddik, Mukhtar, Mohamed Nagy, Effat Nagy/Saad al-Khadem and al-Nasr - this museum is not named, so the narrower window (opening 10:00) is used with the same closed days. Status: youm7 feature of 28 Nov 2025 (open museum); no 2026 closure found. The judge's name varies in sources (Fakhr al-Din / Ibrahim ibn Luqman). Phone on the official page (343763) lacks a current area-code format, not used. Photos: the old house (entrance, court); the Louis IX figure is not used. Ramadan exception dated 2027-02-08 to 2027-03-08: expected Ramadan 1448 AH (IslamicFinder and hijria.com Egypt calendar: 1 Ramadan = 8 Feb 2027, 29 days, Eid al-Fitr 9 Mar 2027); update when officially announced.
